findings.reason: the author must keep a broader pattern and the reader's pattern side by side (or assert against a known-skipped file), otherwise the section converts a measurement into a restatement of the reader it is meant to check.
findings.text: §12(a) narrows the census's directory count to the reader's own `plan-*.v*.json` glob, but the count exists precisely so it can differ from the reader's enumeration (a record the reader skips shows as a difference); with the same glob the two counts are equal by construction and the emitted "equal to the reader's count, so no record was skipped" claim can never fail

findings.reason: the section's own requirement that a record stored before the change still be found at the same path cannot hold unless the author parameterises the suffix length or shares only the validation regex; as stated the store's keying silently changes.
findings.text: §12(d) states that plan_review_path extends review.py:review_path's ".at-<sha> suffix and its validation", but review_path mints `.at-{full-sha}` (review.py:1228, `suffix = f".at-{head_sha.lower()}"`) while plan_review_path mints `.at-{blob8}` (plan_review.py:349, `f".at-{blob.lower()[:8]}"`); the two share only the validation regex `[0-9A-Fa-f]{7,64}`, so extending the rule as written changes the suffix and relocates every stored record

findings.reason: the design should resolve the week through velocity's resolver, or expose a public entry over it for interface_counts to consume, rather than re-deriving the week in the review composer and emitting a count the surface contradicts.
findings.text: §13 attributes "the current week's four interface counts" to interface_counts.py, which counts one named revision and resolves no week (count_revision_cached takes a sha); the week-to-revision resolution the composer needs is owned by velocity.py (`_first_parent_head` at velocity.py:614, used by `_interface_week_rows` at velocity.py:2504), so a composer that picks its own revision (e.g. main HEAD) cites a figure that disagrees with the weekly number the velocity view publishes

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §12 and §13 extend existing modules (census.py, plan_review.py, review.py, recovery.py) behind their current interfaces; neither adds a module nor spreads new shallow wrappers over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §13 resolves "the current week's" interface counts through interface_counts.py, but the week-to-revision resolution it needs is owned by reckon/velocity.py.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §12(a) reuses the reader's `plan-*.v*.json` glob in census.py where the count must stay broader to remain a cross-check, and §12(d) cites review.py:review_path's sibling rule as shared with plan_review_path although the two mint different suffixes.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §13's interface_budget item extends the existing item set and prompt rather than layering a parallel rubric, and §12(d) extends review.py:review_path instead of minting a third path rule, which is the justified direction.
